mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 3%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate by 0.2 percentage points within a month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when UNRATE increases by 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year growth in real sales (RSAFS) below 2% indicates weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when RSAFS growth is below 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1000 units signals a weakening housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when HOUST is below 1000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Negative year-over-year growth in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when INDPRO growth is negative, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive but inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3%, it indicates stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 0% and CPIAUCSL YoY growth > 3%
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL meet the trigger, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 per month signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are negative in more than 40% of cases when PAYEMS growth is above 150,000, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, if the federal funds rate exceeds 4%, it signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If SPX returns are positive in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4%, the hypothesis is rejected.
